fieldworkDocument.title: Measgaichte / Miscellaneous
fieldworkDocument.note: [NOTES: some notes added (most probably by K. D. MacDonald?). See below for details.]

item.description: warp and weft.
leftovers of wool.
threads which were left over at the end of a bit of cloth.
the flyer on a spinning wheel.
after carding this word could be applied to an amount of wool that had been carded. [NOTES: corrected to ‘peàrta’.]
a wooden plank with legs. Had a pin in the middle of this plank, round which wool was wrapped until you had a hank of wool.
tubers on the bottom of a loch. The root of this was used for black dye.

two bits of wood crossed together in the centre. There is a pin in the centre and on the ends of each bit of wood. The wool was wrapped round this until you had a hank. Unlike the ‘crois iarna’ [q.v.] this did not have legs.
onion peel, boiled with salt and used as a yellow dye. [NOTES: ‘rusg’ corrected to ‘rùsg’.]
a pain / palpitation in the chest. The ‘duilleag’ was a certain part of the chest which the informant cannot specify. The pain was similar to indigestion but was more acute.
appendicitis.
gall stones.
rheumatism / sciatica. Cured by seal’s oil which was either rubbed in or drunk.
rupture.
a ruptured muscle, especially in the form of a lump on the back of a hand. Also applied as the term for varicose veins. [NOTES: ‘feith’ corrected to ‘fèith’.]
a bit of wood on a dibble, on which pressure was applied when making a hole for the potato seed.
rotted.
“Brollach an eich is màs na làir.” – a term used when buying horses. Whereas the strength of the male was the important criteria, the width of a mare’s shoulders was equally important.
the term applied to the seeds once they had dried.
the fire in a kiln.
a form of gruel made from small oats.
chaffing.
an unsuitable, lumpy addition. For example this would be applied to a badly made mould board (bòrd-ùireach). [NOTES: corrected to ‘geilcein’.]
reef.
spindthrift [sic] [spindrift?].
swamp.
the gurnet.
periwinkle.
